questions.solution_text:
The histogram has most values in the shorter-time bins and a tail stretching to the right. Box plot $B$ has a much longer right whisker and a median closer to the lower quartile, consistent with this shape.
The values must also agree. With $19$ values, the median is the tenth value. There are $8$ values below $15$ and $13$ below $25$, so the median lies between $15$ and $25$. This agrees with $B$'s median of $18$ and rules out $A$'s median of $27.5$.
For example, the data $10,10,11,11,12,12,13,14,16,18,20,22,24,26,28,30,36,40,50$ give the displayed bin frequencies and $B$'s five-number summary $10,12,18,28,50$.
Box plot $B$.
